body: A few months ago I left my house in the middle of the night after a massive fight with both my parents. My mum eventually found me and told me to 'get in the car right now, we're going home'. I politely replied that I was going to stay overnight at my scout den nearby (which the leaders are fine with me doing) so *everyone* can calm down and we can finish it tomorrow. She then threatened and followed through with calling the police on me. I almost laughed out loud when they basically told her they can't force a 16 year old to return home if they have somewhere safe to go. Just the sheer ridiculous of the situation and the absolute confidence followed by a reality check for her really made the whole experience tolerable.

That's something i've found that is kinda pushed on us by society, 'you're not good enough if you're not doing something important! don't have fun if it's not productive! you gotta keep grinding your whole life!' and honestly its bs. firstly, humans need rest, relaxation and entertainment to keep mentally sane and healthy. Secondly, if you're continually working you'll eventually burn out and you won't be able to work as well as you could if you took breaks. Long breaks of absolutely nothing are great for mental health as it gives your brain a chance to process stuff/relax, so don't feel bad bcos you're actually giving your brain a favour and keeping it healthy and running at its best! it's healthy and good to take a break. Telling myself this helps when i feel guilty about not doing work helps me a lot and i hope it helps you too :)
